MISM 6202 — Foundations of Data Analysis for Business | prerequisites, offerings, professors (Northeastern)

NU Map is an independent, student-built planner — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data comes from the public catalog on a schedule; confirm with the official catalog and an advisor.

3 semester hoursGraduateLectureusually offered: fall, springtypical days: TBostonOnlineOnlineTraditional

Covers basic principles and techniques of descriptive and predictive analytics. What are the essential data analysis concepts underlying business analytics? Topics include descriptive statistics, data visualization, probability and modeling uncertainty, sampling, estimation and confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, simple and multiple regression analysis, time-series analysis, and forecasting. Emphasizes an understanding of how these tools can support decision making and analytics initiatives in a business context with real-world examples and case studies. Uses various software packages for analyzing data sets and creating visualizations.

All course titles in one file: https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/courses/titles.json.
  • Programs (majors and minors, requirements): https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/programs/index.json — look up the program's own URL there, never guess slugs.
  • NUpath attributes: https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/nupath.json · Professors: https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/professors.json (an index by first letter of name).
